status: successor — documents the REAL grader image that implements jinn.grader-context.v1 (issue #2543). NOT yet the deployment's hashed identity: swe-rebench-v2-deployment.mjs still hashes the v1 descriptor, so this file changes no consumer. Adopt by pointing the .mjs's descriptor path at this file once the org ratifies the container-grade cutover — see `selection`.
graderReportSource: container — the deployment module constructs its own containerGraderReportSource over the daemon Docker driver (createDockerContainerRuntime). The digest-pinned image the adapter runs is a REAL swe-rebench grader image (operator/deployments/evaluator/swe-rebench-v2-grader/): built per instance FROM that instance's published swe-rebench eval image, it reads the jinn.grader-context.v1 context file, verifies the declared subject digests, applies the Result subject (candidate patch) to /testbed, applies the baked gold test patch, runs the declared fail-to-pass and pass-to-pass node ids with the instance's real pytest, and leaves grader-output.json (upstream report-item shape) on the writable bind-mounted workdir, which the adapter reads and parseSweRebenchReport scores.

graderImage.note: There is exactly one grader image PER swe-rebench instance, because the shipped jinn.grader-context.v1 context file conveys neither the transitions nor the gold test patch nor the instance identity — those are baked into the image at build time (/jinn/grader/manifest.json + /jinn/grader/test.patch). A single generic grader image cannot satisfy the shipped contract; that is a property of the schema, documented in the grader README. The image reference is not carried here — it lives per instance in EvaluationSpec.familyBlock.image, set by the minting pipeline to the grader image (which transitively pins the instance image) rather than the raw instance image.

verdict.pass: every declared fail-to-pass transition now passes and no declared pass-to-pass transition broke
verdict.fail: at least one declared transition did not hold
verdict.ungradeable: the grader could not determine the transitions (e.g. pytest missing, patch did not apply, container crash) — never a failing verdict, the attempt is retried

scoring.rule: passed = every fail-to-pass node satisfied AND no pass-to-pass node broken

isolation.rationale: unchanged from v1 — the swe-rebench-v2 grade path writes into the image rootfs at grade time (the base eval image's Python site-packages), which lives on the rootfs, not under the writable bind-mounted workdir. A read-only rootfs would break any instance whose grade touches site-packages. Because the driver also runs the grader with `--network none`, the grader performs NO package installs at grade time and relies on the eval image being fully provisioned (the sweb.eval.* images are); a genuinely pytest-less image is classified ungradeable:pytest_missing. The container is still resource-capped and confined (--network none, --cap-drop ALL, --no-new-privileges, --pids-limit, --memory, --cpus, noexec/nosuid /tmp) per the driver defaults.

selection: The deployment module (swe-rebench-v2-deployment.mjs) hashes exactly one sibling descriptor into evaluationMethod.digest. It hashes v1 today, so v1 remains the deployment's committed identity and every existing consumer (and the swe-rebench-deployment.test.ts guard) is unaffected. Cutover to container grading is a one-line change — point that readFileSync at swe-rebench-v2-evaluation-method.v2.json — done deliberately when the org ratifies the swap, together with a minting pipeline that sets EvaluationSpec.familyBlock.image to grader images built by the tooling above. This descriptor is additive and inert until then.
evidence: the adapter attaches the (tail-capped) test log as claim evidence; the deployment's evidenceWriter is a real, durable content-addressed filesystem repository
